name: Mucinous adenocarcinoma of the appendix

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for appendiceal mucinous adenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of mucinous adenocarcinoma with extracellular mucin production and invasive glandular structures in appendiceal tissue
Radiological evidence of appendiceal mass or mucocele with features suggestive of malignancy on CT or MRI
Presence or absence of pseudomyxoma peritonei on imaging or surgical exploration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mucinous adenocarcinoma in appendiceal tissue with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical biopsy; imaging alone is insufficient for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Mass often corresponds to appendiceal tumor or mucocele
searchTerms: palpable lump in lower right abdomen
mass felt in right lower belly

pathognomonic.notes: Mucinous ascites due to peritoneal spread of mucinous tumor cells

common.symptomName: Chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain
searchTerms: long-term pain in lower right belly
persistent pain in right lower abdomen

common.notes: Due to mucin accumulation or tumor mass effect
Secondary to bowel obstruction or irritation

occasional.notes: May be related to tumor-associated inflammation

searchTerms: altered frequency or consistency of stools

occasional.notes: Due to mass effect on stomach or bowel

searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen without liver problems
ascites not caused by liver disease
abdominal fluid accumulation unrelated to liver

rare.notes: Due to tumor invasion or external compression
Secondary to ureteral compression by tumor mass
Due to lymphatic obstruction from tumor spread

imaging: CT scan showing appendiceal mass or mucocele with irregular wall thickening
genetic: GNAS mutations associated with mucinous tumors

distinguishingFeatures: Benign cystic dilatation of appendix without invasive adenocarcinoma
Absence of cellular atypia on histology
Usually secondary to mucinous appendiceal tumors but can arise from other sites
Diffuse mucinous ascites with peritoneal implants
Requires identification of primary tumor for definitive diagnosis

redFlags: Unexplained persistent right lower quadrant mass
